headline: A senior adviser at the investment firm KKR argues in Fortune that AI has not yet sped up economic growth because companies are slow to reorganise around it.
score_reason: Pool 4 kept: the full commentary was read; it is one investor's opinion with no new event, so it stays on the watchlist.
importance_line: What changed is an argument, not new evidence: one investor's view that AI's economic payoff depends on companies redesigning their work and may take a decade or more, which matters first to workers and employers deciding how fast to restructure, then to investors weighing the AI boom, and the doubt is that it is an opinion built partly on the author's own measure of company overhead.
summary: Fortune publishes a commentary by Ming Lu, a senior advisory partner at the investment firm KKR, arguing that AI is spreading quickly among consumers but has not yet made the economy grow faster because companies have been slow to redesign their work around it, a gap he calls the Innovation Paradox. He cites McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey, in which 88% of organisations use AI in at least one function but only 6% report an AI effect of more than 5% on earnings before interest and tax (EBIT), and argues from earlier technology waves that the full payoff usually takes more than ten years.
notes: Read in full (fulltext). Opinion commentary by Ming Lu; Fortune says commentary views are the author's own. Published 11 Oct 2026.
